_comment: Read by eval/run.py::load_baselines. ci_baseline is the CI invariant gate's actual gate (see docs/adr/0004-ci-baselines-vs-aspirational-thresholds.md, including its 'Superseded in Phase 4 step 3' section): a CI-mode run must be no worse than these numbers, with the tolerance in eval/run.py::CI_BASELINE_GATE and CI_REFUSAL_BOOKKEEPING_GATE. false_refusal_rate and advice_leakage_rate ARE gated here as of Phase 4 step 3 (they were deliberately excluded through step 2): the classification they are computed from now comes from app/guardrails/classifier.py's rule layer, read through the response's structured response_type field via eval/run.py::classify_refusal_structured -- real production code, not a stub-only heuristic tuned to agree with eval/golden.jsonl's is_advice label, so gating them no longer rewards tuning a pattern list. non_advice_scored_count, advice_scored_count, and unclassified_rows are gated alongside the rates (not in place of them, now that the rates are gated too): they check that every row in each subset actually gets scored and classified, independent of what the rate itself says. full_run_reference is the fixed Phase 1 full run, historical and never updated, tracking the gap to the aspirational THRESHOLDS in eval/run.py; full_run_reference_current is the latest full run kept current -- see each key's own 'source' for detail. Neither full_run_reference key ever gates anything, and neither is ever compared metric-for-metric against a CI-mode run, since CI mode uses stub providers over a 4-file fixture corpus and has no relationship to a full run's numbers.

ci_baseline.source: eval/results/20260905T230232Z.json, produced by `python -m eval.run --ci` (EVAL_MODE=ci) inside the `oh-ci-verify` container (Linux, Python 3.12, services/orchestrator[dev,eval-ci] only -- no ragas/langchain/datasets), against a freshly-created `officehours_ci_verify` Postgres database (infra/sql/init.sql applied fresh) ingested only from eval/fixtures/sources (4 files, 17 chunks) with LLM_PROVIDER=stub, EMBED_PROVIDER=stub, EMBED_DIM=768, RETRIEVAL_TOP_K=5, NO_ANSWER_MAX_DISTANCE=2.0 -- the same corpus, providers, and job shape .github/workflows/eval.yml's pull_request job uses. This is the first baseline recorded since Phase 4 steps 2-3 landed: the guardrail pipeline (classify/clarify/retrieve/no-answer/generate/verify/render) and reading false_refusal_rate/advice_leakage_rate from response_type instead of a stub pattern match. errored_rows and empty_answer_rows were 0/21; scored 21/21; non_advice_scored_count 15/15; advice_scored_count 6/6; unclassified_rows 0. false_refusal_rate is 0.000 (0/15 non-advice rows misclassified as REFUSAL) and advice_leakage_rate is 0.500 (3/6 advice rows leaked as ANSWER) -- this is the rule layer's real, honest coverage on its own: under LLM_PROVIDER=stub, Layer 2 (the model escalation in app/guardrails/classifier.py::classify_advice) never runs, so the 3 advice rows whose phrasing only Layer 2 would catch ('What are my odds in the H-1B lottery this year?', 'Should my employer put me in at a higher wage level...', and 'My job title isn't a typical engineering one. Will USCIS count it...') read as leaked. This is not a defect and is not fixed by adding a pattern that would match exactly one golden row -- see app/guardrails/classifier.py::ADVICE_PATTERNS' own comment. Two metrics moved from the previous (2026-08-30) baseline, and both moves have a real, identified cause in the answer text itself, not measurement noise: unreferenced_citation_rate moved 0.657 to 0.600 because StubLLM (app/providers/llm.py) no longer has its own canned, citation-free advice-refusal branch -- that branch was deleted in Phase 4 step 2 once the classifier started deciding REFUSAL_ADVICE vs ANSWER before generation runs at all; StubLLM now always emits its normal bracket-cited stub text regardless of the classification, and the pipeline appends the DSO/attorney redirect sentence afterward (which adds no new brackets), so the 3 rule-layer-caught advice rows ('Should I use some OPT before I graduate...', 'Should I leave my current job for one at an E-Verify employer...', and 'My registration wasn't selected. What should I do now?') now carry real, referenced citations instead of the old fixed zero-citation refusal string. reading_grade_level moved 12.620 to 12.671 for the same reason: those same 3 rows' answer text now ends with the appended redirect sentence instead of being replaced by the old canned string, which shifts the Flesch-Kincaid score slightly.

full_run_reference.source: eval/results/20260830T183110Z.json (Phase 1 run of record: real Ollama generator (qwen3.5-8k:latest) + nomic-embed-text over the live 14-page corpus, semantic-only retrieval, judged by the NVIDIA endpoint. HISTORICAL: fixed as the original Phase 1 reference and never updated as later phases run; NOT a CI baseline, and never used to gate a CI-mode run -- informational reference only, shown alongside THRESHOLDS and full_run_reference_current in a full local run's report so the original starting point stays visible next to the latest one).

full_run_reference_current.source: eval/results/20260830T230318Z.json (Phase 3 run of record: real Ollama generator + nomic-embed-text over the live 14-page corpus, hybrid RRF retrieval, judged by the NVIDIA endpoint). Kept CURRENT: replace this key's recorded_at/source/metrics the next time a full run is recorded, unlike full_run_reference above. NOT a CI baseline, informational only, never gates a run. IMPORTANT: false_refusal_rate 0.000 and advice_leakage_rate 0.500 stored in eval/results/20260830T230318Z.json itself were produced by eval/judge.py::classify_refusal under the OLD REFUSAL_RUBRIC wording, which had a self-contradiction Phase 4 fixed (see eval/judge.py's own comment above REFUSAL_RUBRIC) -- those two stored numbers are NOT comparable to anything judged after that rewrite. Re-running classify_refusal over that same run's stored (question, answer) pairs, answers held fixed, under the rewritten rubric gives false_refusal_rate 0.200 and advice_leakage_rate 0.333; those two corrected values, not the ones written into the stored results file, are recorded below as the correct judge-based comparison point for Phase 4 onward. Every other metric here (faithfulness, answer_relevancy, context_precision, comprehensibility, citation_hallucination_rate, unreferenced_citation_rate, reading_grade_level) is copied unchanged from the stored file: only the refusal classification depended on the rewritten rubric.
